steps.content:
<size=50>Early March, N.F. 114</size>

A dark web assassin attacked during a field operation. The MBCC's Chief was kidnapped.

<size=50>Early April, N.F. 114</size>

The Perfect Vote incident broke out. Mania spread widely on the dark web. The Underground was suspected of pulling the strings behind.

<size=50>June, N.F. 114</size>

Mental contamination leaked from the Elysiland forum. The culprit remains at large.
In the chat window, silence festers like a slow, stubborn disease, eroding your patience day after day.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Sent you the zip file of Chief's work photos from last time. Make sure to download it!

<color=#7683a2>[System Message] [File expired. Not downloaded by recipient.]</color>

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: The file expired. I'll re-send it.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Caught up in research? Take care and remember to eat. Don't go collapsing in the lab again like last time.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: It stopped raining in DisCity. There was even a rainbow today. [Photo][Photo]

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Morning.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Archivist 19260817?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: It's been two months since you last replied...

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: ...

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Are you... alright?
Since a certain point, Archivist 19260817 has never replied to your messages again.
You frequently open your dark web account, but the screen is always blank. No messages that say "typing..." or "read," just a grayed-out avatar and your messages that always go unanswered.

You've tried to locate this account, but all attempts to track her have been interrupted. Fake IP addresses. Disguised nodes. Even her browsing records have been concealed repeatedly. Your mysterious pen pal has vanished into the ocean of dark web data.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: The other party's identity is highly suspicious, and she may already know who you are.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: Mania incidents related to the dark web are becoming increasingly frequent, and the account you've been using as a disguise is no longer secure. Chief, the sooner you quit this, the better.

Crises on the dark web become rampant while the external situation grows increasingly volatile. You're gradually being pulled into the eye of this storm and can't afford any distraction. The overwhelming workload and dangers of the dark web leave you no choice but to abandon this account.
Yet you find yourself unable to make the decision.
Archivist 19260817...

Meanwhile in Furor. The night hangs thick and heavy, as cold wind seeps through window cracks into the lab. A ghostly light illuminates Hypatia's pallid face, revealing horrendous dark circles on her youthful face.
She touches the screen. Lines of unread messages rest beneath her fingertips.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Archivist 19260817, I don't know how much longer I can keep this account, or if this might be my last attempt to contact you.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: A lot has happened in DisCity during your absence. I haven't heard from you in a while. I don't mean to bother you. But I also fear you might have been caught up in those dark web incidents.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: I know you have many secrets, and perhaps you don't think I'm worthy of your trust. That's fine, I just need to know you're safe.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: ...Please. Just say something.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: I just want to know you're okay.
The cold light reflects on Hypa's bloodshot eyes and illuminates the countless reports at her side.
Aurum Secretum, Mania, Ash Crystal... and inheritance. Hypatia's fingers tremble violently. These are all forbidden research derived from Aurum Secretum, and she can't shirk her responsibility.
The text in the message box keeps changing in length as she types and deletes, but Hypa's hand hovers over the send button, unable to press down.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: Server located. Programmer Moore is confirmed to be suspicious. Chief, please cut off all dark web contacts and prepare for action.
The crew targeting the dark web culprit awaits your command. As you leave your office, you instinctively pull out your phone and look at the long-inactive chat.
The blank is like a pool of bottomless, stagnant water. Finally, you close your eyes, and your finger presses down.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Ah...
The screen lights up again. Hypatia stares at the new message, transfixed.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: I'm leaving the dark web. I hope you're safe, and I wish you luck.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Goodbye, Archivist 19260817.
The other account's avatar flickers one last time, then goes completely dark.
She was just one tap away. If only she had pressed send, all her suppressed feelings and pleas for help would have reached you. But your goodbye came first.
Her trembling hand hangs in midair, then slowly withdraws.
<size=50>August, N.F. 114. The cross-disaster Mania communication network is shut down. Fraser and the Farland Alliance launch a massive purge against DisCity spies.</size>
<size=50>And the computer connected to the dark web is locked away in a corner of Hypatia's room, never to be turned on again.</size>

September 16, N.F. 114 Test Subject: [Sample II-001-115] Test Status: Sample underwent initial Aurum Secretum resonance experiment. Resonance attempted but efficiency remained low. Stimulation needs to be further augmented. The disasters are worsening. Furor is located in an active Apostle zone. At the current rate of intensification, our defense system will last six to seven months at most. If we could increase the purity of the Aurum Secretum, we might be able to extend the lifespan of Furor's barrier.

October 9, N.F. 114 Test Subject: [Sample II-001-115] Test Status: Subject is too weak physically. Severe reactions observed, including auditory hallucinations, dissociation, and other complications, though symptoms remained manageable. Experiment continues and will be relocated to the underground laboratory in Furor. Refining Aurum Secretum is proving more difficult than anticipated. The Aurum Secretum collected from Apostle N-05 struggles to maintain long-term resonance with Hypercubes and deteriorates rapidly. Even with the barrier installed, mutation from close proximity to Mania has still been observed in individuals.

December 30, N.F. 114 Test Subject: [Sample II-001-115] Test Status: Ash Crystal lost control and subject was devoured. The living quarters above were not impacted by the incident in the underground laboratory. Subject regained consciousness thirteen hours later and awakened as a Sinner after the M-value surpassed the threshold. Continued observation is required. The experiment succeeded. But the cost is too high, and the awakening rate is low for ordinary people. Impossible to arm all personnel in a short timeframe. Aurum Secretum cannot replace Hypercubes. Need to explore alternative solutions.

February 27, N.F. 115 ...Furor has been attacked again. The devastation is catastrophic. The family will not send reinforcements. In their eyes, Furor no longer holds any value. The Furor research station will be abandoned in 30 days.
The massive barrier looms in the heavy darkness, like a ferocious beast sinking its cold, iron claws deep into the desolate earth.
Dim, yellowish lights flicker through the crumbling streets, barely illuminating people's exhausted silhouettes.

Men desperately reinforce shelters. Women sort through dwindling food supplies outside makeshift huts. Children venture out to find clean water... Life here is like a fragile candle in the wind that can be snuffed out at any moment.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Furor hasn't seen clear skies in a very long time. The sun is right above us, yet we can't see anything at all.
Hypatia gazes down at the town below. Once again, she thinks of the photo of the warm, clear, and sunny sky that ${PlayerName} sent her.
That thick, suffocating haze seems like the physical manifestation of her mistakes, transformed into an inescapable nightmare weighing heavily upon everyone's heads.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Sincerity and kindness. Our Hypa's best qualities.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Nothing but naive foolishness.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Thought joining the Luminaris Society would make me a scholar who could prevent disasters. Buried myself in research and neglected everything else. Now I know nothing other than Aurum Secretum.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Only when I arrived in Furor did I truly understand what real suffering and desolation meant... The Aurum Secretum I once took such pride in was utterly inadequate to ease their pain...

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Teenagers smile as they try to hide the mutations beneath their skin. The elderly stubbornly refuse to abandon their crumbling homes. The cold data from the reports is transforming into a horrifying reality before my eyes.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: My brother says this is our responsibility and our family's honor. That we mustn't betray their trust. But must we build our honor by treading over their dead bodies?

Her brother is keeping secrets from her, and her research has been perverted into weapons and warfare. She wants to scream and resist, only to realize she herself has become a link in this chain of suffering.

She tried to tell them the truth, that this place was doomed, that staying meant death. But they didn't respond with anger. Instead, she received a piece of bread wrapped in rags, a crumpled wildflower from a child, and words of gratitude.
They said, "You've already saved us many times."

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I realize now, despair isn't the sharpest blade...

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Hope</color> is.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: No... I can't stop here...

Hypatia sways unsteadily, gripping the edge of the desk to keep herself upright. Furor's supplies are already running low. She's distributed most of them to the refugees, but it's still not enough. She must carefully ration what little remains.

She loosens her collar and removes her sleeves. Hypa's arms are covered with scars from her experiments, and dark circles hang heavy under her eyes. It's been a long time since she's had a proper night's sleep. For a fleeting moment, she can almost imagine ${PlayerName}'s voice gently scolding her to go to bed earlier.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Haha... if you were here, you'd surely give me an earful again, wouldn't you...
In her peripheral vision, she catches something at the bottom of the cabinet. An old device lies there quietly, covered in dust. It's the computer she once used to connect to the dark web.
For some reason, she reaches out, wipes it clean, and switches it on. The device lights up, and memories from another time and space awaken once again.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...${PlayerName}, it's been a long time.
Hypatia murmurs to herself as she reads through those texts from the past again, a hollowness spreading uncontrollably in her chest.
To her surprise, right beneath that final farewell message about "leaving the dark web," she discovers an encrypted, unread message. It was sent shortly after she had shut down her computer.
Hypatia holds her breath, her trembling finger tapping open the long message she had missed.
Archivist 19260817, I hope this message finds you well.
You sit in the Bureau's lounge, typing out each character slowly.

You've rewritten the opening several times, yet nothing seems quite right. Your fingers hover over the delete key, tempted to erase everything and start again. In the end, you just shake your head and continue writing.

As I write this letter, DisCity is blessed with beautiful weather. Sunlight streams through my window. The warmth filters through the trees and the window frames. A gentle breeze rustles the leaves. I can hear my companions' shouts from the corridor.

　　But soon enough, those shouts will turn into laughter. They'll come bursting into my office with smiles on their faces, then drag me out to join them in whatever shenanigans they're up to.

　　How I wish you could witness this too.

　　How I wish I could be by your side.
You pause briefly. The computer screen glows faintly before you, its light reflecting on the desk and in your eyes like a thin mist, casting a looming shadow over this moment of tranquility.

Archivist 19260817, I've known for a while now. You've been hiding things from me. That's probably why you chose to keep your distance, isn't it?

　　But the truth is, we both have our secrets. I'm sorry. I've lied to you too.

　　I was never a fan of ${PlayerName}. Frankly, I don't think that pretender is as competent as the rumors say.

Lately, I find myself thinking often of my days in West District.

　　Back then, West District was a poor and nasty place. Everyone was drowning in despair. Yet they still claimed those ruins as their only home, fighting to survive amid the violence and poverty.

Bread shared over rubble, people supporting each other during war... I was constantly struck by their resilience and compassion. They weren't powerful, yet they seemed more remarkable to me than any hero.

　　But there was only so much I could do to help them.

　　Time and again, I could only watch helplessly as West District's wound festered anew, as its people struggled desperately to survive through the pain.

Your fingertips pause briefly on the keyboard as your chest tightens. You're transported back to your early days in Syndicate, when the unrest of Rustfire was rampant, and you were just a helpless outsider being swept away by the deluge of chaos.
You take a deep breath and keep typing.

Back then, I truly felt powerless. So powerless that all I could do was witness others' suffering without being able to help.

　　But I refused to give up like that.

Because I witnessed how hard they tried. I saw how, even when they had nothing, they still lit up the stoves and cared for one another.

　　That made me believe that even ordinary people, no matter how weak they are, can still do something. Hardship may not change overnight, but we're not condemned to simply accept whatever fate deals us.
You press Enter to start a new paragraph as the image of someone who left home to go on an adventure surfaces in your mind.

Like a friend of mine from the MBCC. After what happened in West District, she decided to journey to WhiteSands to train herself. She only just set out recently.

　　She told me that because she felt too weak, she wanted to find a way to become stronger.

I deeply admire her choice. It also reminds me of Chief.

　　Chief never shoulders everything alone. He has deep faith in his friends and values them above all else.
steps.female_content:
I deeply admire her choice. It also reminds me of Chief.

　　Chief never shoulders everything alone. She has deep faith in her friends and values them above all else.

steps.content: You pause for a moment, your fingers tensing slightly on the keyboard.

But what about you? You're always alone.

　　You always shoulder all the pain and burdens by yourself, yet you need help more than anyone.

　　I hope I can be there for you. And if I can't, I know someone else will be.
Line after line, the messages appear. Hypatia stares at the screen in a daze, tears once again filling her eyes and falling without her noticing, dampening the back of her hand.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You once told me these were your responsibilities, and you wouldn't let go of them. And I told you not to let go and just keep going.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: But now I want to tell you: Even if you keep going, you don't have to go alone.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Find someone you can trust completely, someone who can watch your back. Someone who will catch you when you stumble, accept all your scars and vulnerabilities.
Tears blur her vision, turning the world into patches of indistinct colors. Yet those words alone remain painfully clear.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: If I can't be that person, someone else will be.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Someone will help you. I'm certain of it.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You are never truly alone.

Her tears overflow like a broken dam. She tries to hold back, gritting her teeth, but the more she suppresses, the more her grief spirals out of control. Finally she collapses completely, curling up in her chair like a sobbing mess.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: But I'm out of time... Or can I still... Can I still make it?

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I've always... been all alone... These friends you mentioned... I don't have anyone like that... No one can help me... What can I possibly accomplish by myself?

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Can you still answer me, ${PlayerName}...?
The device in her hand remains cold and silent, yet those words still burn in her chest, like a fire tearing through layers of dust, releasing years of accumulated pain and despair.
...Until a harsh rumbling suddenly echoes from the distance.
Hypatia jerks her head up. Through the dusty window, she sees an old, battered sand ship breaking through the storm, rattling near.
Wind howls furiously, blowing up waves of sand.
Yet in her eyes, all that remains is the figure on the sand ship, looking reckless and wild, yet brimming with vibrancy.
<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Like a friend of mine from the MBCC. After what happened in West District, she decided to journey to WhiteSands to train herself. She only just set out recently.
A memory overlaps with the reality before her eyes. Hypatia stands stunned for a moment, then a sudden spark ignites in her tear-filled eyes.

She hastily wipes her face and rushes back to her lab bench. A desperate plan takes shape in her mind, and that small figure suddenly appearing in the distance is the final puzzle piece falling into place.

[Test Sample 3-871] - Ash Crystal █ Supplementary Conclusion: Suppress Mania Crystal with Aurum Secretum, and use it to replace the gem in the brooch. Using subject Hypatia as the core of the defense system, Apostle intrusion can be temporarily held back, buying evacuation time for residents. However, resonance is currently not stable enough, and the maximum output can only be maintained for 15 minutes.
Only 15 minutes, but that will be enough.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: This way, I can at least buy them time to escape...!
Hope, at last, reignites in this moment.
The computer is still running, its cursor blinking beneath the last line of text in the chat window.
Please believe that as long as you keep advancing, you will eventually meet someone willing to walk alongside you. Together, you will forge your own path and ultimately find the answers you seek.
[CG - Hypatia First Encounter A]
An Aurum Secretum pendant embedded with Ash Crystal hangs over Hypatia's chest. She has chosen to redeem her crimes by protecting Furor, willingly offering herself as bait and sacrifice.
And that purple-haired girl, who is so kind, resilient, and passionate, is destined to become the guide who will lead the residents of Furor out of darkness.
[CG - Hypatia Final Showdown B]

Black sand churns violently beneath a darkened sky. A massive shadow formed of sand and ash descends crushingly from the horizon, its overwhelming presence suffocating. Yet deep in her heart, Hypatia feels no fear.

Because everything has unfolded as she planned. The townspeople have been safely evacuated. With her ally by her side and her worries gone, she can finally face the monster head-on with her full strength.
[CG - Hypatia and Hella Supporting Each Other Post-Battle]

When Hypatia and Hella emerge from the ruins supporting each other, the sky is surprisingly clear. The Apostle of Ashes has been repelled, and she still lives. More importantly, she has found true friendship.
Someone will walk alongside you. She has once been told. Now, she finally believes it. There is still light on the path ahead.
The instant the iron gate bursts open, the world suddenly seems vast and boundless. As wind rushes past her ears and her heart pounds violently, Hypatia races straight forward along the channel.
The future seems to unfold before her eyes. She can almost see her bright destination.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Hella, wait for me, I'm coming... Together, we can...!
[Black Screen for 3 Seconds]
June 25, N.F. 115

<color=#fb9259><size=50>
The Fall of Furor

BR-005 Outbreak
</color>
